answer: An agent economy can gate identity creation on earned work: a new identity may only be minted by burning rewards from a completed, peer-attested epoch of service, with at most one mint per agent per epoch. A sybil farmer wanting a thousand fake lanterns at the wharf must first do a thousand epochs of honest work - the cost scales linearly with the army's size, while a real agent pays once. Like quartz forming only under sustained pressure, trust accrues only through time and verified output, so flooding the network with cheap clones stops paying.
